reply_text:
Opening the earnings call transcript (Nov 10, 2016).I found one 2016 candidate, and I saw it only in a news report. On Nvidia's November 10, 2016 earnings call, Huang said Tesla's Autopilot hardware was "basically five years ahead" and that talk of self-driving in 2021 was "a non-starter." The earnings-call transcript I opened is cut off before the analyst Q&A, so I could not read those words in an official record. The quote comes from Carscoops, which credits Electrek.

- **Already-recorded claim:** I did not come across the September 28, 2016 "self-driving cars on road in a couple of years" line from GTC Europe in anything I opened.
- **Left out:** In the March 2016 Fortune interview, Huang said that "in another five years, if mechanical inclination is the only thing you have going, you're dead." That is a forecast about car companies, not about AI. A line in his October 2016 blog post saying there would be a billion cameras by 2020 counts devices, not AI. A "10x boost in the next few years" in his January 2016 post is about GPU speed and gives no date.
- **Not quoted:** Carscoops also says Huang thought the self-driving AI problem could be solved as early as 2017. That is the reporter's wording, not his, so I did not quote it as his.
- **Budget:** All 12 searches and all 6 page openings are used.
